Hi Emily —

Great to hear — we can absolutely provide a concise ramp plan + checkpoints. I sketched a focused 6-week approach below (short bullets you can paste into procurement):

Week 0 (pre-implementation):
- Confirm production traffic profile + representative prompts (we only need ~10–20 prompt examples and a token distribution).
- Agree on success metrics: 95th pctl latency target, cost per 1k tokens target, and SLO for error rate.

Weeks 1–2 (observe & baseline):
- Deploy initial small pool (dev tier) with conservative batching and full precision model.
- Collect per-route token histograms and KV cache hit rates.
- Deliver Baseline Report + recommended batching window and cache TTL.

Weeks 3–4 (optimize & validate):
- Apply KV/prefix caching for stable prompt prefixes and enable continuous batching.
- Test two quantization profiles (int8 and mixed-8) on a canary subset; measure quality delta on your evaluation prompts.
- Introduce routing fallback policy: route to lower-cost variant when latency budget allows.

Weeks 5–6 (rollout & economics):
- Roll recommended quant profile cluster-wide if quality within agreed thresholds.
- Autoscaling policy tuned to observed 95th pctl.
- Final Cost/Performance Playbook delivered and one final rollback runbook.

Checkpoints for procurement (examples you can include):
- PO #1: Initial deployment capacity (dev pool) — triggers at signed contract.
- PO #2: Canaries pass (quality + latency) — triggers move to production pool.
- PO #3: Scale + reserved capacity (optional) — triggers if 30-day sustained throughput exceeds X

I've attached a short cost-profile template and our quant profiles summary for your eng team. Ben, Karthik — can you add any technical constraints I missed?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Marissa / team —

Small technical addendum for the plan above (keeps procurement-aware language separate from implementation notes):

Observability & data we need (Week 0):
- Example prompts (10–20), average and p95 token lengths, and expected concurrent requests.
- Any downstream SLAs (e.g., banking latency constraints) that influence 95th pctl target.

Batching/caching specifics (Weeks 1–4):
- Start with micro-batching window 5–10ms to preserve latency for small payloads; increase to 20–30ms for longer sequences after validation.
- KV cache TTLs: set default 30s for prefix-stable flows; extend to 5m for known session flows.
- Enable prefix-level cache keys for any prompt templates — we’ll provide a short regex guide.

Quantization profile tests (Weeks 3–4):
- Test INT8 and mixed-8 on a 2k-request canary. Measure BLEU/SUF/EM- style deltas (or your eval metric).
- If quality delta > 2% on critical prompts, fall back to full precision for those routes.

Routing policy examples:
- RouteByLatency: if 95th pctl < budget, send low-cost variant 40% of requests for sampling.
- FallbackOnError: automatic route to higher-fidelity model on generation errors >0.5%.

I’ll prepare the small regex guide and the canary runbook; Marissa, if you want I can join the kickoff call for the first data handoff.

-Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
